name: אַחֵר
summary: Aher is named once, in the genealogies of Chronicles: “Hushim, the sons of Aher” (1Ch 7:12), at the end of the list of Benjamin. The name is spelt exactly as the adjective אַחֵר, “another, other”, the word Eve used of Seth, “another seed in place of Abel” (Gen 4:25), and Rachel of the son she asked for (Gen 30:24). Scripture does not explain the name, and the verse is short enough that it can also be read “the sons of another”, with no man named at all.

evidence.note: חֻשִׁם בְּנֵי אַחֵר: “Hushim, the sons of Aher”, the only place the name stands.
The word the name is: זֶרַע אַחֵר, “another seed in place of Abel”.
“May Yahweh add to me another son (בֵּן אַחֵר)”: the same word of a child hoped for.

note: BDB key a.cp.ai is spelt like the adjective, so its 49 tokens are every singular אַחֵר; only 1Ch 7:12 is the name. Whether אַחֵר here is a name or the adjective (“the sons of another”) is open; Hushim is the son of Dan in Gen 46:23, which some take to be meant here. Not followed further.
